definition: GPTZero is an artificial intelligence detection software developed to identify artificially generated text, such as those produced by large language models.
details: While GPTZero was praised for its efforts to prevent academic dishonesty, many news outlets criticized the tool's false positive rate, which can be especially harmful in academic settings.

explainer.lead: GPTZero is software that examines writing and assesses whether it was generated by artificial intelligence, including text from large language models. It can help educators investigate academic dishonesty, but a mistaken accusation can have serious consequences.

tiers.eli5: GPTZero is like a writing detective that looks at an essay and guesses whether a person or an AI wrote it. Its guess can be wrong, so it should not be treated like a camera that caught someone cheating.
tiers.practitioner: GPTZero is applied to passages of text when reviewers want an indication of possible AI generation, particularly in academic-integrity checks. Treat its output as one piece of evidence rather than a verdict, and account for false positives before taking action.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, GPTZero can be described as a detector f: T -> A, where T is input text and A is an assessment of whether the text was artificially generated. A documented limitation is its false-positive rate: human-written text may be assessed as AI-generated, which is especially consequential in academic settings.

explainer.example: A teacher submits a student's essay to GPTZero after suspecting that a large language model wrote it. If the software assesses the essay as AI-generated, the teacher still needs to consider that it could be a false positive before concluding that the student cheated.

usedIn.name: GPTZero
usedIn.detail: AI-detection software for examining text that may have been produced by large language models.

usedIn.name: Academic integrity
usedIn.detail: Used as part of efforts to identify artificially generated writing and prevent academic dishonesty.

explainer.intuition: The basic idea is to inspect a piece of writing for indications that it was generated artificially rather than written by a person. The result is a detection assessment, not direct proof of who or what produced the text.
howItWorks: A user provides a passage of text to GPTZero.
The software examines the writing for indications of artificial generation.
It returns an assessment of whether the text appears to have been AI-generated.
A reviewer interprets that assessment while allowing for the possibility of a false positive.
explainer.whyItMatters: GPTZero addresses concern about AI-generated text being passed off as a student's own work. Its false positives matter just as much as its detections, because human writers can be wrongly suspected of academic dishonesty.
misconceptions: An AI-generated assessment is not conclusive proof of academic dishonesty.
GPTZero detects possible AI-generated text; it does not generate or improve the writing itself.
